summary.headline: EID Parry Q2 FY27: sugar realisation rose to INR45.11/kg from INR40.67, with sales of 84,000 MT vs 73,000 MT a year earlier.
summary.overview: Sugar volumes and realisations both improved YoY in Q2 FY27, with sugar revenue of about INR486 crores vs INR368 crores. Crushing ran 66 days (vs 48) on 4.03 LMT cane crushed, though recovery eased to 7.86% from 7.97%. Distillery output fell to 307 LL from 392 LL, and realisation dropped to INR63.99/litre from INR67.55. The consumer products (CPG) turnover fell to about INR120 crores from INR165 crores as low-margin categories were exited, while value-added product share rose to 28% from 16%. Management guided to an at-par FY27 vs FY26 across sugar, distillery and co-gen, and flagged a 10% lower Karnataka cane crop next year.

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: Crushed 4.03 LMT over 66 days (vs 3.66 LMT over 48 days); recovery 7.86% vs 7.97%; produced 32,000 MT sugar vs 27,000 MT. Sales of 84,000 MT at INR45.11/kg.

segments.name: Co-generation
segments.commentary: Generated 385 LU (vs 307 LU), exported 175 LU (vs 128 LU). Tariff INR3.73/unit vs INR4.04/unit; revenue INR17.67 crores vs INR11.94 crores.

segments.name: Distillery / alcohol
segments.commentary: Produced 307 LL (vs 392 LL) and sold 440 LL (vs 409 LL), of which ENA 212 LL and ethanol 234 LL. Realisation INR63.99/litre vs INR67.55; segment revenue INR305 crores vs INR291 crores.

segments.name: Consumer products (CPG)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR120 crores vs INR165 crores, due to lower bulk dal and white sugar sales. Management says margins improved QoQ; VAP share rose to 28% from 16%. Still loss-making, with breakeven targeted for FY28.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: Indian operations turnover INR10.26 crores (vs INR7.6 crores); consolidated turnover about INR70 crores (vs INR61 crores). Strong H1 and Q2 driven by US subsidiary Valensa International (prostate, joint, derm/hair care, greens).

segments.name: PSRIPL (refinery subsidiary, SEZ)
segments.commentary: All inventories sold and cash realised as of September 30. Final SEZ duty payment expected in Q3 FY27; duty liability already provided as of March 31, 2026. Asset monetisation to start after SEZ and environmental clearances.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sugar, distillery and co-gen performance expected to be at par with FY26, per Ashiq J. A. H.; management declined to give formal guidance and will update in Q3.
Ethanol volume for FY27 guided at about 14 to 15 crore litres (ENA plus ethanol), largely molasses-based; the same range expected in subsequent years.
Consumer business breakeven targeted for FY28. A TV interview reference to INR500 crores revenue this year was raised by an analyst; H1 was about INR200 crores.
Institutional sugar contracts are now 15 to 24 days; the team is mirroring spot prices. About 96-97% of long-term contracts are completed.
Next year's Karnataka cane crop estimated about 10% lower, with sowing possibly down 8-10%.
capex_capacity: No capex or inorganic plans in the sugar and biofuel business, per Muthiah Murugappan.
Non-core asset monetisation: PSRIPL refinery physical assets being divested; asset sales to follow SEZ and environmental clearances.
No capital allocation planned for nutraceuticals; consumer business needs opex (A&SP, manpower, NPD) rather than capex, with capital allocation expected in the FMCG segment.
Grain ethanol supplied from the 120 KLPD grain facility at Sankili, Andhra Pradesh, which will continue.
Exploring bagasse-based green grow media / substrate business, which has been commercialised; no biochemical plans for now.
demand_pricing: Global: white sugar rose from about $467/t in July to $518/t in September; raw sugar from about $0.148/lb to $0.179/lb. Global surplus of about 1.1 MMT in '25-'26 expected to turn to a deficit of about 0.2 MMT in '26-'27.

India: SY25-26 closing stock of 3.7 MMT after 31 MMT gross production, 3.1 MMT ethanol diversion, 28.5 MMT consumption and 0.8 MMT exports. Government steps (duty-free raw sugar imports, dealer stock limits, quota releases) moderated ex-mill prices by quarter-end.
Cane price in North Karnataka is about INR3,800/t, against FRP of about INR3,300-3,400/t. All FRPs were paid on time.
Ethanol allocation formula gives roughly 35-40% of base ethanol volumes; some volume shifting to ENA.
Tamil Nadu cane volumes are running 8-10% higher this year, but Karnataka has the better margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Karnataka and Maharashtra crop shortfall due to yields or sowing, and will next year's output be hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashiq Hashim said the crush season is 10-15 days shorter after an 8-10 day late start, mainly due to water availability. Sowing could fall 8-10%, and the company estimates a 10% lower crop next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 ethanol volume given the loss of B-heavy and juice feedstock?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 14 to 15 crore litres for FY27, largely molasses-based, with some volume shifting to ENA; grain ethanol comes from the Sankili facility.

qa_highlights.question: Will the second half combined across sugar, distillery and co-gen beat last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects an at-par year versus last year. Venkateshwarlu said it is too early for formal guidance and would update in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook and capital allocation for the consumer business and nutraceuticals, and for refinery and non-core asset sale proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: CPG is targeting breakeven in FY28 and needs opex rather than capex. Nutra has no capital allocation plans. Refinery asset divestment is ongoing and proceeds are to strengthen the standalone balance sheet, with capital likely going to FMCG. No buyback is under discussion.

qa_highlights.question: How are institutional sugar contracts structured, and how quickly are spot price moves passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term contracts are mostly gone (96-97% completed). Current contracts run 15-24 days and track spot prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why not diversify into biochemicals or bio-CNG to cushion the sugar cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashiq J. A. H. said options are being evaluated but nothing is imminent. The company is not exploring biochemicals, but is pursuing bagasse-based green grow media.

risks_watch: Karnataka and Maharashtra cane shortfall (about 10% lower crop estimated) and possible sugar imports in SY26-27.
Ethanol allocation uncertainty: volumes depend on government formulas, and FY27 is guided at 14-15 crore litres.
Farmer agitation and pending committee policy on cane pricing; cane prices above FRP may squeeze margins.
CPG remains loss-making, with breakeven targeted only for FY28 and revenue falling YoY.
Q3 watch items: final SEZ duty payment for PSRIPL, asset monetisation timing, and formal FY27 guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on sugar realisations and the global price recovery, but cautious on the Indian crop outlook and FY27 guidance, which management declined to give beyond at-par. Evasive on refinery duty quantum and biochemical diversification, deferring both.
key_quotes: We would estimate an at par year compared to last year.
Our estimate is about a 10% lower crop for next year. That's the estimate.
Most of our contracts may be, at best, even with our prime customers, be for about 15 days to 24 days, not more than that.
There are no capex or inorganic plans in the sugar and biofuel side.

growth.why: Management guided FY27 sugar, distillery and co-gen to be at par with FY26 and declined formal guidance, with no capacity additions and no capex in sugar or biofuel; the Q2 sugar revenue jump (INR486 crore vs INR368 crore) rests on higher price and volume, not new capacity.

oneOffs.what: Year-ago Q2 was not described as weak or disrupted; crushing ran 66 days vs 48 but this is a seasonal/operational volume swing, not a one-off

quality.why: Sugar revenue rose about 32% (INR486 cr vs INR368 cr) from both volume (84,000 MT vs 73,000 MT, about +15%) and realisation (INR45.11/kg vs INR40.67, about +11%), but the brief names no one-off items, and the growth is largely recurring. The Q2 base, however, reflects a longer crush (66 vs 48 days), which is an operational swing rather than a one-off, and the CPG decline (INR120 cr vs INR165 cr) i

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided FY27 sugar, distillery and co-gen profitability at par with FY26, and cane landed cost rose to INR3,798/MT from INR3,620/MT while distillery realisation fell to INR63.99/litre from INR67.55, offsetting the sugar realisation gain to INR45.11/kg from INR40.67.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management said there are no capex or inorganic plans in sugar and biofuel, and grain ethanol continues from the existing 120 KLPD Sankili facility, so no new capacity is signalled.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Sugar sales rose to 84,000 MT from 73,000 MT, but a 10% lower Karnataka crop next year and FY27 ethanol guided at 14-15 crore litres (at par) cap volume growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management stated no capex plans for sugar and biofuel and no capital allocation for nutraceuticals, while utilisation was not disclosed, so no new capex is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided only an at-par FY27 versus FY26 and declined formal guidance until Q3, with a 10% lower Karnataka cane crop flagged for next year.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cautious on the Indian crop, with cane prices around INR3,800/t against FRP of INR3,300-3,400/t and sowing possibly down 8-10%, which could squeeze margins; formal guidance is due in Q3.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Exploring a bagasse-based green grow media business that is already commercialised, but no timing or size was given, and biochemicals are not being pursued.

rows.label: PSRIPL SEZ final duty payment and refinery asset monetisation
rows.why: Final SEZ duty payment is expected in Q3 FY27 with liability already provided at March 31, 2026, and asset sales follow SEZ and environmental clearances, so timing of monetisation is still open.

rows.label: CPG breakeven
rows.why: CPG is still loss-making with turnover down to INR120 crore from INR165 crore, though VAP share rose to 28% from 16% and margins improved QoQ, and breakeven is targeted for FY28.

rows.label: Sugar price pass-through via 15-24 day contracts
rows.why: Long-term contracts are 96-97% completed and current institutional contracts of 15-24 days track spot, while global white sugar rose to $518/t in September from $467/t in July, supporting realisations.

tone.note: Management was confident on sugar realisations and the global price recovery but cautious on the Indian crop and declined formal FY27 guidance beyond at-par; analysts pressed on the Karnataka crop shortfall, ethanol volumes, and CPG and refinery timing.
